concepts.title: Why Organisms Reproduce
concepts.definition: Reproduction is the life process by which organisms produce more of their own kind, ensuring the continuation of species generation after generation; it can create identical copies or varied offspring, shaping both survival and evolution.
concepts.key_idea: No reproduction, no future: the process carries life across generations.

solution_steps.explain: Reproduction produces new individuals of the same kind.

concepts.title: Asexual Reproduction
concepts.definition: Asexual reproduction needs one parent and gives offspring identical to it: bacteria split by fission, yeast buds, planaria regenerates from fragments, and plants multiply through runners, cuttings or spores - fast, but without variety.
concepts.key_idea: One parent, identical copies: fission, budding, regeneration and spores cover the modes.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc111.txt sections on asexual reproduction modes

solution_steps.explain: No gametes or partners are involved.
Fission, budding, fragmentation, regeneration or spore formation.
Genetically identical clones result from the division.

concepts.title: Sexual Reproduction in Plants and Animals
concepts.definition: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and specialised sex cells or gametes: in flowering plants pollen carries male gametes to the ovule for fertilisation, forming seeds, while in animals including humans male and female gametes fuse to form a zygote that grows into a new individual - mixing heredity to create variation.
concepts.key_idea: Two gametes, one zygote: sexual reproduction mixes heredity and breeds variety.

The gametes fuse into a zygote with mixed heredity.
